notes: The NP *priHóm h₁nómn̥ 'dear / own name' = Ved. priyáṃ nā́ma = OE frēo-nama. Scholarship: Scheller 1959 (Vedisch priyá- und die Wortsippe frei, freien, Freund, p. 68–76), reported by Schmitt 1967 §97 and §373 ('Laut für Laut entspricht dieser Wendung das altenglische freo nama') and West 2007 ch. 10 with n. 76 ('etymologically identical'). Caveat carried from Schmitt §97: a secure IE idiom, 'doch wohl noch lange nicht ein Bruchstück poetischer Phraseologie'; Scheller glosses *priHó- as 'eigen' (one's own), and the OE word means 'surname, cognomen' (Bede: freónama glosses cognomento), so 'dear' in the English is the Vedic sense; the inherited sense may be 'own, proper name'. Revised after round 4: cut to the NP, as an np utterance in the accusative (r4: the verb was stitched from a plural-object stanza and 'begot' fits neither text). Case: both branches have the NP as an accusative object (RV 10.84.5c VedaWeb ACC SG with gr̥ṇīmasi; Crist 636 freónoman, n-stem acc. sg., object of cende); the neuter has nominative = accusative, so the printed form is the same. Loci checked locally: RV 10.84.5c priyáṃ te nā́ma (acc. sg. n., the case of the line), RV 10.123.7d nā́ma janata priyā́ṇi (pl.), RV 7.56.10a priyā́ vo nā́ma (pl.), all in VedaWeb; OE Crist 636 freónoman cende in Grein's Bibliothek (Exeter Book, the only manuscript; Grein's apparatus has notes on 635 and 641 but none on 636, so freónoman is the manuscript reading, not an emendation). The OE word is univerbated (Bosworth–Toller hyphenate freó-nama): both members are cited as lemmas, frēo (< *frija- < *priH-o-, Kroonen s.v. *fri(j)a-) and nama (< *namon-, Kroonen). Formation: OE has a compound, Vedic a syntagm; the members are the same lexemes. No verb: none is shared. RV 10.123.7 has janata (thematic injunctive middle 3sg, VedaWeb) with the plural object, RV 10.84.5 gr̥ṇīmasi 'we praise', RV 7.56.10 huve 'I call'; in Crist 636 the subject is Job and the object Christ, so cende is cennan II 'declare, proclaim' rather than cennan I 'beget' (Bosworth–Toller file it under I), and either way the formation differs (Ved. thematic middle, OE causative). Caveat (Schmitt §97): a secure idiom, not necessarily poetic phraseology; the OE witness is a Christian poem. Local-source recheck (2026-10-25): OE Bede 2.5 is present in oe-bibliothek-ags-prosa/bibliothekderang0004chri_djvu.txt (Bibliothek IV); OCR has freonama Oesc in the genealogy of Æthelberht. The Bede reference remains support only.
